apps.description: A free, open-source two-factor authentication (2FA) app with an encrypted vault.
features: Unlock with a password or biometrics
Add entries by QR code, image or by hand
apps.long_description:
Aegis Authenticator generates the one-time codes that online services ask for as a second step when you sign in. It supports the industry-standard HOTP and TOTP algorithms, so it works with thousands of services, and it is compatible with Google Authenticator.

Your codes are kept in an encrypted vault (AES-256-GCM) that you unlock with a password or with biometrics. The app can block screen capture and hide codes until you tap to reveal them.

New entries can be added by scanning a QR code or an image of one, by typing the details in, or by importing from other authenticator apps. Entries can be sorted, grouped, searched and given custom icons, and the vault can be exported or backed up automatically to a location you choose.
apps.name: Aegis

features: Photo and video viewer for many formats
Basic editor: crop, resize, rotate, flip, draw, filters
Remove EXIF metadata such as GPS location
Recycle bin to recover deleted items
apps.long_description:
Fossify Gallery is a photo and video app that says it has no ads and no unnecessary permissions. It opens a wide range of formats, including JPEG, JPEG XL, PNG, MP4, MKV, RAW, SVG, GIF and AVIF.

A basic editor lets you crop, resize, rotate, flip and draw on photos and apply filters. You can strip EXIF metadata such as GPS coordinates and camera details, and protect chosen photos and videos, or the whole app, with a PIN, pattern or fingerprint.

Deleted photos and videos go to a built-in recycle bin so you can recover them. The look of the app and its function buttons can be customized, with Material Design dynamic themes and custom themes.

apps.description: An open-source, all-in-one retro game emulator for Android, built on Libretro.
features: Automatic save states, quick save and load
apps.long_description:
Lemuroid is an open-source emulation app for Android based on Libretro. Its main goal is ease of use, good Android integration and a great user experience.

It scans and indexes your game files, saves and restores game states automatically, and supports zipped ROMs and gamepads. It can simulate LCD or CRT displays, and offers local multiplayer, tilt input, customizable touch controls and optional cloud save sync.

According to the project page, supported systems include Atari 2600, 7800 and Lynx; NES, SNES, Game Boy, Game Boy Color and Game Boy Advance; Sega Master System, Game Gear, Genesis and Sega CD; Nintendo 64 and Nintendo DS; PlayStation and PSP; Neo Geo Pocket; PC Engine; WonderSwan; and arcade games through FinalBurn Neo. You supply your own game files.
apps.name: Lemuroid

apps.description: An open-source Material Design file manager.
features: FTP, SFTP, SMB and WebDAV servers
Custom colors and a true-black night mode
apps.long_description:
Material Files is an open-source file manager for Android 5.0 and later. It follows Material Design closely and aims to be lightweight, clean and secure.

Besides browsing local storage with breadcrumb navigation, it can view, extract and create common archives, and view and manage files on FTP, SFTP, SMB and WebDAV servers. With root access it can also manage files that need it.

Like the Nautilus file manager on Linux, it understands symbolic links, file permissions and SELinux context. Colors are customizable, and there is a night mode with an optional true black.
apps.name: Material Files

apps.description: An Android port of the melonDS Nintendo DS and DSi emulator.
features: Can be launched from third-party frontends
apps.long_description:
melonDS for Android is a port of melonDS, an emulator for the Nintendo DS and DSi. You supply your own game files.

According to the project, performance is solid on 64-bit devices with threaded rendering and JIT enabled. Older 32-bit devices run much slower because JIT is not supported there.

Other launchers and frontends can start melonDS once it has scanned the ROMs. The project lists local multiplayer, DSi SD card support, customizable button skins and more display filters as features it does not have yet.
apps.name: melonDS

apps.long_description:
NewPipe is a free, lightweight front-end for video and audio streaming services. It fetches data from each service's official API, or reads the website when that is not possible, so you do not need an account on any service.

It uses no proprietary libraries such as Google Play Services, so it can run on devices without Google apps.

It currently supports YouTube and YouTube Music, PeerTube, Bandcamp, SoundCloud and media.ccc.de, with YouTube the best supported. The project describes the app as beta.

It supports many app sources, including GitHub, GitLab, Codeberg, F-Droid, IzzyOnDroid, SourceHut and direct APK links. Crowdsourced app configurations are available on the project's website.

For some sources the data is gathered by scraping web pages, which can break when a site changes its design.
